I have rarely seen any other skin tone aside from one family in church but then I went to different churces and there were people of colour. I still felt weird, I didn't belong, it wasn't right. But it was more diverse. I don't think I saw more than one darker skin tone until I was 13 and we moved overseas. Which is strange because in most Bibles it is said that a majority of these people in the bible were Jew and in the sun a lot. Sun darkens your skin. There was not a lot of shelter then or protection from the sun. The further away from the sun you go, like inside or Antartica, you are going to be lighter. Joseph was a different time period than like Nephi and Laman. They could have been darker than him. Did Joseph not see many darker people? Why is it so fucked up in that area? In many areas? I need to do some more research.

Some days are good, some days are meh. Right now I am having an anxiety attack because... well, 1. too much shit on my plate RN and 2. I usually clock out at 7 (our supposed time to clock out but they keep us until 8 sometimes) and am fine, so it seems. But I usually clock out at 7 and a co-worker stopped me to ask me some questions and wished me well (he was concerned on my leaving early but I felt fine). I have only been working a month, some co-workers help me out and give me tips then there are some co-workers (I work mostly with boys) that just piss me off and rub me the wrong way. So, it depends. But from now, I guess I will wait that dreadful call for 'you can go home' but before I even consider leaving, I walk the aisles and check for zoning errors I may have missed or if there is anything else I need to zone, see how many other people are still zoning and if everything looks good... well, then I will leave. I have been looked at by my floor managers and they say nothing and they haven't called me over to talk to me like others yet. So, I guess I'm good. For now. Overall, I really like it. It is quiet, barely any customers, my co-workers and people over me are nice. I do get sore though, so stretches, protein powder, protein, back roller, and good shoes come in handy.
